data.command: Explain T1547 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution

data.text:
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ cat /usr/share/doc/mitre-attack/techniques/T1547.txt
T1547 - Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
Tactics: Persistence (TA0003), Privilege Escalation (TA0004)
Platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, Network, Containers, ESXi, IaaS, Office Suite

Adversaries configure system settings to automatically execute a program
during system boot or when a user logs on. Autostart mechanisms are native
to the operating system or bundled with installed software, so abusing them
lets an adversary keep access across reboots and, where the mechanism runs
under a privileged context, escalate privileges.

Common autostart locations on this platform (Linux):
  ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.profile, /etc/profile.d/.sh
  /etc/rc.local, /etc/init.d/, systemd units (/etc/systemd/system,
    ~/.config/systemd/user), cron "@reboot" entries and /etc/cron.
  XDG desktop entries in ~/.config/autostart/ and /etc/xdg/autostart/
  PAM module stacking (pam_exec), /etc/ld.so.preload, kernel module autoload

Windows equivalents: Run/RunOnce registry keys, Startup folder, Winlogon
helper DLLs, Services, Security Support Providers, LSA authentication
packages, time providers, active setup, print monitors/processors, bootkit.

Sub-techniques:
  T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
  T1547.002 Authentication Package
  T1547.003 Time Providers
  T1547.004 Winlogon Helper DLL
  T1547.005 Security Support Provider
  T1547.006 Kernel Modules and Extensions
  T1547.007 Re-opened Applications
  T1547.008 LSASS Driver
  T1547.009 Shortcut Modification
  T1547.010 Port Monitors
  T1547.012 Print Processors
  T1547.013 XDG Autostart Entries
  T1547.014 Active Setup
  T1547.015 Login Items

Detection:
  Audit changes under /etc/systemd/, /etc/init.d/, /etc/cron.*, /etc/profile.d/
  and each user's ~/.config/autostart/ and shell rc files. Baseline these
  paths, alert on new units/services, and watch for processes whose parent is
  an init or login-time daemon but which never appear in a clean baseline.
  auditd watches on /etc/passwd, /etc/ld.so.preload and unit file writes help.

Mitigations:
  M1013 Application Developer Guidance
  M1018 User Account Management
  M1022 Restrict File and Directory Permissions
  M1024 Restrict Registry Permissions
  M1040/M1047 Audit and least-privilege enforcement on autostart paths

Reference: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/
webapp@web-srv-01:~$
